text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a sharp 99th pctl latency cliff (~200ms -> ~1.8s) on shared-gpu pool-B starting 12:34 UTC. Looks correlated with a burst of long-seq requests from small tenants :eyes: grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd

aj: Which tenants and which model?

maria: t-omega and t-sparrow mainly, both low qps (2-5 rps) but many long sequences. KV eviction rate shoots up during the window.

raj: Attaching quick profiler/kernel-selection excerpt from the affected host:
```
[12:34:21] kernel_select: model=rw-v2-13b seq=8192 -> chosen=fast_attn_v1
[12:34:22] kernel_switch: fallback=quant_attn_v1 (reason=alloc-fail, mem_pressure)
kv_cache: evictions=1275/s (slot_range=0-4096)
batcher: prefetch_window=16 -> enqueued_prefetch=1200
```

leo: Host perf stats: nvlink_bandwidth=95%, gpu_mem_avail=3.2GB, host_mem_pressure=high, kv_eviction_latency_ms=8.1. Also saw kernel compile churn around same time.

infra-bot: autoscaler: burst pool-B requested +2 nodes at 12:36 UTC, nodes registered at 12:36:27 (scheduling lag 27s).

ops: Hypothesis: aggressive prefetch (prefetch_window=16) queued lots of KV slots, pushing active KV working set over capacity. That triggered mass evictions, kernel fallback due to mem fragmentation, and a long-tail latency for small requests — noisy-neighbor effect.

aj: Can we reproduce in canary? Try lowering prefetch_window to 8 on one host and observe. Also collect kv slot histograms + batch size distribution.

maria: Quick A/B: changed prefetch_window=8 on a single host in pool-B and replayed a small load — 99th went from ~1.8s -> ~360ms within 2 minutes. Median unchanged. So prefetch aggressiveness seems causative.

raj: Filed INF-9321 with artifacts and traces. Short-term mitigations proposed:
1) Set prefetch_window=8 for shared pools (hotfix)
2) Add per-tenant prefetch throttle when kv_evictions/s > 500
3) Improve autoscaler alerting on kv_eviction_rate and kernel_fallback_rate
4) Add a canary that simulates many concurrent long-seq small tenants for regression tests

leo: Pushing hotfix to pool-B (rolling restart of prefetch workers) in 10m. Will monitor 50/95/99 and kv_eviction_rate.

infra-bot: hotfix deployment started at 12:46:00 UTC, rollout to 12/18 hosts in pool-B (strategy=conservative).

ops: Follow-up: create a perf regression test suite that exercises mixed workloads (small-tenants long-seq + bursty short requests) and assert 99th < 500ms under target capacity. Add to CI and run weekly.

maria: Thanks — once hotfix stabilizes attach pprof + perf traces to INF-9321 and we can schedule a deeper root-cause (kernel selection heuristics + kv prefetch interaction).

infra-bot: hotfix completed at 12:49:30 UTC; monitoring shows 99th back near 350ms and kv_evictions down to ~180/s. Keeping alerting on for 1h. :thumbsup:
